answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price identity with a stake-and-slash bond: each agent locks collateral before transacting, and peers attest its work the way a sparrow vouches for a flockmate. Reputation then flows like a river — trust earned slowly through verified deliveries, never bought in bulk. A juniper stake planted per identity makes mass forgery expensive: ten thousand sock puppets means ten thousand locked bonds, and proven fraud burns the bond. Honest agents pay once; attackers pay linearly, so forgery stops scaling.
